<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The top-level scope of this PKGBUILD consists only of standard variable assignments: pkgname, pkgver, pkgrel, pkgdesc, arch, url, license, depends, makedepends, conflicts, options, source, and sha256sums. The source entry is a single tarball reference (with an HTML-escaped quote in the original, which is a benign formatting artifact) and the sha256sums contains a real checksum; neither involves command substitution, network calls, eval, or any executed payload at source time.

There are no top-level $(...) or backtick command substitutions, no curl/wget/git invocations, and no file writes outside the normal makepkg flow in the global scope. The executable content (prepare, build, package) only runs when makepkg invokes those functions, which is explicitly out of scope for this ``makepkg --printsrcinfo`` gate and will be reviewed in the full audit.

No genuinely malicious behavior is present in the portion that executes during ``makepkg --printsrcinfo``. The file passes this narrow safety gate.
</details>
<evidence>
</evidence>
<summary>
Top-level PKGBUILD scope contains only safe variable definitions.</summary>
</security_assessment>

<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
This .SRCINFO file is a standard, benign AUR package metadata descriptor for the neodisk disk space visualizer. It declares the package version (2.83.2), license (GPL-3.0-or-later), dependencies, and a single source pointing to the project's official upstream repository at github.com/tkslucas/Neodisk, pinned to a specific release tag (v2.83.2).

The `>` characters visible in the depends lines (e.g., `gtk4>=4.14`) are simply XML entity escaping of the `>` character that appears in the source text itself; in the actual .SRCINFO they represent normal version constraints (`gtk4>=4.14`).

There are no indicators of malicious behavior: the source is fetched from the project's own upstream over HTTPS, the source is pinned to a specific tag rather than a mutable branch, and a valid sha256sum is provided for verification. The file contains no executable code, no obfuscation, no eval/base64/curl patterns, and performs no file operations or network exfiltration. This is purely declarative packaging metadata.
</details>
<evidence>
</evidence>
<summary>
Standard AUR metadata, upstream pinned source, valid checksum.
</summary>
</security_assessment>

The sha256sums field provides a checksum, verifying source integrity. No external network transfers occur during the build phase; only the initial git clone is performed from the same host. Build commands (swift package, swift build, patchelf) are typical for Swift projects and do not execute arbitrary code. No use of eval, base64, curl, wget, or other suspicious constructs. Installation steps copy files to standard system directories with appropriate permissions. No data exfiltration or unauthorized system modifications are present. Hence the package is safe.
</details>
